findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware writes vCenter events to vmware:events, not vmware:vc:event. Splunkbase 5380 is 'Mattermost Alerts', not a VMware forwarder add-on. Both errors repeat in app, references, and detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215, https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3215) for `vmware:vc:event` ... Also Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere Forwarder (Splunkbase 5380
findings.suggested_fix: Use sourcetype vmware:events from Splunkbase 3215 (or vmware_inframon:events from 5089), and drop every 5380 reference.

findings.explanation: vSAN 7.0 Update 1 is the release that introduced the deterministic reserved capacity for internal operations and host rebuilds, replacing the old fixed ~25–30% slack guidance. The text moves that feature to 7.0 U3 and 8.0 and invents an 'SPBM-driven auto reservation' for 7.0 U1.
findings.quote: on 7.0 U1 the platform moved to SPBM-driven, policy-mixed auto reservation ... On 7.0 U3 and 8.0 you see operations reserve and host-rebuild reserve as separate accounting items
findings.suggested_fix: Say that from vSAN 7.0 U1, reserved capacity is split into an operations reserve and a host-rebuild reserve and calculated deterministically, and that before that release the guidance was 25–30% slack.

findings.explanation: vSAN space usage is normally read through the vSAN Management SDK (VsanSpaceReportSystem.VsanQuerySpaceUsage), not a public vSphere Automation REST path. This endpoint, /cluster/{cluster}/host, /health, /api/vcenter/vsan/clusters, and event IDs such as com.vmware.vsan.health.test.cn.clusteryellowred.* all look invented.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the vSAN Management API reference. Either cite the real method names or present these paths as wrapper endpoints of a customer-built poller.

findings.explanation: Troubleshooting items g through m refer to host_rebuild_pct, largest_host_used_bytes, eta_to_full_h, dedup_ratio_drift, and dedup_ratio_baseline, none of which the SPL produces (it uses eta_full_days and dedup_drift). They also suggest widening a match() regex the SPL does not use (it uses like()), and cite unrelated controller-HCL test IDs.
findings.quote: check `largest_host_used_bytes` in the HEC body ... `eta_to_full_h` jumps from null to 168h ... `dedup_ratio_drift` ... widen the `match()` regex
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite items g through m to use the SPL's field names and the like() filter, or delete them.

findings.explanation: This leaks an authoring instruction into reader-facing text. The snippet also calls undefined helpers and mixes a SOAP session key with the legacy /rest base path.
findings.quote: Python (outline, ~90 lines, no inline comments in production code per your build rule
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the build-rule aside, and either complete the helper functions or label the snippet as pseudocode that uses /api/session and the vmware-api-session-id header.

findings.explanation: The description and controlTest list null guards as triggers. The real alerts are a red health test, usable_used_pct at or above t_crit (default 90), negative host-rebuild headroom, or an ETA to full under 7 days (critical), with lower bands at 80 and 70.
findings.suggested_fix: State the severity ladder from the SPL in the description and controlTest.

findings.explanation: azure, github, and the equipment model cisco_aci have nothing to do with vSAN capacity.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep vmware (and vxrail if intended), and remove azure, github, and cisco_aci.

findings.explanation: The HEC reference is truncated, and there is no VMware or Broadcom reference for the vSAN capacity or reserve model the UC relies on.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the HEC page and the Broadcom TechDocs page on vSAN capacity reservations.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, yet it cites an unrelated app and sourcetype and relies on REST paths that cannot be confirmed, so no SME verification is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the status until the poller contract is confirmed against vCenter.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `dedup_enabled` defaults to "true" when the field is missing, so every cluster reports dedup_enabled=1. `headroom_for_host_rebuild_bytes` subtracts the largest host's raw capacity rather than the data it holds, which overstates the rebuild requirement on lightly used hosts.

The base search pulls vmware:vsan:health and vmware:vsan:diskgroup over 25 hours only to drop them at the next `where sourcetype="vmware:vsan:capacity"`. The health data is fetched again in the join subsearch, so the base search does unnecessary work.

summary: The capacity reasoning is strong: usable versus raw capacity, host-rebuild headroom, and a worked example. But the UC cites Splunkbase 5380 (an unrelated app), a vmware:vc:event sourcetype the VMware add-on does not emit, and wrong vSAN reserve-model history. The REST endpoints look invented, and the troubleshooting section refers to fields the SPL never produces.
